acceptance_criteria: AC-1 _move_note_to_history appends to an existing history file and never truncates one.
AC-2 A note that is exactly the self-referential pointer for that id is not written.
AC-3 A test closes an item whose history file holds narrative and whose JSON note is that pointer, and asserts the narrative survives verbatim. The test was observed to FAIL against the pre-fix code.
AC-4 A test covers an item with a real note reaching the file without removing prior content.
AC-5 A test covers note-then-status and asserts the appended note survives.
AC-6 A test asserts the heading status line reflects the new status after closure.
AC-7 python3 -m pytest tests/test_project_queue.py -q passes, with the count reported before and after.
AC-9 The repository privacy gate reports zero findings.
AC-10 The diff touches scripts/project_queue.py and tests/test_project_queue.py only. No project/*.json and no docs/history/backlog/*.md appears in it.

baseline.authority: docs/design/GOV_ORCH_11_CLOSING_AN_ITEM_MUST_NOT_DESTROY_ITS_HISTORY.md -- FROZEN, PRODUCT OWNER APPROVED 2026-09-13. Section 2 is the specification (N-1 to N-5); section 4 is the acceptance. It is short and complete; read all of it.
baseline.test_baseline: python3 -m pytest tests/test_project_queue.py -q -- run it first and record the count before changing anything.
baseline.the_defect: cmd_status, on a move to a terminal status, calls _move_note_to_history, which calls path.write_text(header + note) -- an overwrite. cmd_note appends. _migrate_note_to_history, in the same file, ALREADY appends under a dated heading when the file exists. The correct pattern is therefore already present in this module; _move_note_to_history is the one function that does not use it.
baseline.why_it_loses_data: GOV.ORCH.5 moved open items' narrative out of the JSON and left the note field holding the literal pointer 'see docs/history/backlog/<id>.md'. Closing such an item writes header plus that pointer over the file that holds the narrative. Eight history files were damaged this way on 2026-09-13, on two branches that were discarded rather than merged, so origin/main still holds the narrative.

invariants: No write to docs/history/backlog/<id>.md may reduce that file's information.
A self-referential pointer is never written into the file it points at.
The heading's status line reflects the item's current status after a closure.
No backlog item's status or content changes in this movement.
Redaction still applies to everything written.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review of the diff plus orchestrator verify.passed. The worker does not merge to main.
report.objective: Fix the silent data-loss defect GOV.ORCH_11 names: scripts/project_queue.py truncates docs/history/backlog/<id>.md when an item moves to a terminal status. Make that write append, refuse to write a self-referential pointer, and prove the fix with the regression test the defect would have failed.
output_contract: A write path that cannot reduce a history file, with the regression test that the defect would have failed.
SESSION_CLOSE reporting the test count before and after, the observation that the decisive test failed pre-fix and passes post-fix, and which acceptance item each new test covers.

recommended_reasoning.reason: A small, fully specified change to one function, with the correct pattern already present in the same module, plus four named tests. The contract leaves nothing to decide; the care is in writing the decisive test so it genuinely fails first.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Read GOV.ORCH.11 fully first. Every rule you implement must trace to N-1 through N-5, and each new test must name the acceptance item it covers.
Write the failing test FIRST, confirm it fails against the current code, then fix. Report both observations in your SESSION_CLOSE. A test that has never been seen to fail proves nothing.
Commit early and often: the failing test, then the fix, then the remaining tests.
Do not merge to main. The Product Owner assistant reviews the diff and merges.
Do not run the full pytest suite. It creates untracked data/ and logs/ directories that the repository privacy gate then flags, failing a movement whose diff is clean.
risks: Writing the fix without ever seeing the test fail, so the test proves nothing.
Detecting the self-referential pointer with a loose substring match that also drops a real note mentioning the path.
Appending a second heading block instead of updating the status line in place, leaving two contradictory status lines in one file.
Changing a backlog item to demonstrate the fix, which puts state changes in a tool-fix diff.
Creating a restoration commit for files that were never merged.

in: N-2: make _move_note_to_history APPEND when docs/history/backlog/<id>.md already exists, and create it with the standard heading only when it does not. Follow the shape _migrate_note_to_history already uses in this same module rather than inventing a second one.

N-4: when the file already exists, the heading's 'status:' line must still end up reflecting the item's NEW status. A field is not narrative, so updating it in place is not a reduction. Update that line; do not append a second heading block and do not leave a stale status line.

N-3: a note whose entire content is the pointer 'see docs/history/backlog/<id>.md' for this same id carries no information and must NOT be written into the file at all. Detect it exactly -- do not use a loose substring rule that would also drop a real note that happens to mention the path.

Acceptance test 3, the decisive one: create an item whose history file already holds narrative and whose JSON note is that self-referential pointer, close it, and assert the narrative is still present VERBATIM afterwards, and that the pointer was not appended. The defect would have failed this test; without it the fix is unproven.
Acceptance test 4: an item with a REAL JSON note, closed, whose note reaches the history file without removing what was already there.

Acceptance test 5: the sequence a worker naturally uses -- 'note --id X --text ...' followed by 'status --id X --set done' -- asserting the appended note survives the closure. This is the sequence that lost the data.
A test that the heading's status line reflects the new status after closure (N-4).
out: Changing which statuses are terminal, or TERMINAL_STATUSES membership.
Changing the JSON note field's own lifecycle, or the pointer string it is replaced with after a move. Only the FILE write changes.
Changing cmd_note, _migrate_note_to_history, cmd_migrate_open_notes, or the GOV.ORCH.9 backlog split logic.
Changing redaction behaviour. redact_narrative still applies to whatever is written.
Changing any backlog item's status, content, priority or note. This movement fixes the tool; it closes nothing.
Restoring the eight damaged files. They were never merged; origin/main is intact. Do not create a restoration commit.
Any change outside scripts/project_queue.py and tests/test_project_queue.py.

tests/test_project_queue.py: 4 new regression tests plus one tightened assertion in an existing test. No other test touched.
completed: N-2: _move_note_to_history now appends under a dated heading when docs/history/backlog/<id>.md already exists, following the shape _migrate_note_to_history already used, and creates the file with the standard heading only when it does not exist.
N-3: a note whose entire content is the exact self-referential pointer 'see docs/history/backlog/<id>.md' for that id is detected by exact equality (not substring) and is never written into the file.

N-4: added _set_history_status_line, which updates the heading's 'status: ... . target: ...' line in place on every closure, whether or not the note is the pointer, without duplicating the heading block.

AC-3 (decisive): added test_status_close_with_self_referential_pointer_note_preserves_narrative_verbatim -- seeds a history file with narrative, sets the item's JSON note to the pointer, closes it, and asserts the narrative survives verbatim and the pointer is never written. Confirmed this test FAILS against the pre-fix code.

AC-4: added test_status_close_with_real_note_appends_without_removing_existing_content -- a real JSON note reaches the file without removing prior content. Confirmed this test FAILS against the pre-fix code.

AC-5: added test_note_then_status_done_sequence_preserves_appended_note -- the 'note' then 'status --set done' sequence that lost data pre-fix; the appended note now survives closure. Confirmed this test FAILS against the pre-fix code.

AC-6: added test_status_close_updates_status_line_in_place_without_duplicate_heading, and tightened the pre-existing test_status_transition_to_terminal_moves_note_to_history assertion from 'status: done OR status: in_progress' to require 'status: done' and require the stale 'status: in_progress' line is gone.
